reading.body:
Google's Council Bluffs campus in Pottawattamie County is part of the company's largest aggregate data center investment in any US state, with over $20 billion deployed in Iowa since 2007. The company does not publish individual building capacity figures for this site, so its MW footprint and current rack count remain unknown. Of the 52 mapped data center facilities in Iowa, only 2 operators have published power specifications statewide, totaling 18 MW in disclosed capacity; this campus ranks third by published MW in its state, a ranking that reflects the incompleteness of public disclosure rather than measured facility power.

Google announced a $7 billion expansion for the Council Bluffs campus as part of a broader Iowa investment, indicating material growth at this location, though the timing and phasing of deployment are not published. The company has secured a power strategy that includes a NextEra Energy agreement tied to restarting the Duane Arnold nuclear plant in Iowa, suggesting an attempt to address grid constraints for future scaling at the campus. Without published MW capacity, the relevance of this site to AI scaling cannot be measured directly from operator disclosure.

The site's constraint on AI relevance is not its location or Google's investment commitment, but the absence of a published power budget. Facilities that do not disclose capacity cannot be ranked against other campuses or assessed for their current or planned role in AI infrastructure. This campus matters to the degree that Google's continued silence on individual building specifications matches a broader industry pattern: most mapped data centers publish no capacity figure at all, making the grid's actual utilization state largely opaque to observers of AI scaling.
